description: Set up and run organizational membership management: database setup, registration processing, member communications, engagement tracking, and renewal handling.

steps.description: Set up the member database with fields for contact info, join date, membership status, groups, and roles.

inputs.name: organization-profile
inputs.desc: Name, type, and size of the organization

inputs.name: membership-categories
inputs.desc: Types of membership offered (full, associate, youth, honorary)

outputs.name: database-schema
outputs.desc: Field definitions and data types for the member database

outputs.name: category-definitions
outputs.desc: Membership categories with rights, dues, and requirements for each

process: Define the core member fields: name, contact info, join date, status (active, inactive, pending), and household grouping.
Add group and role fields: committees, ministry teams, volunteer roles, and leadership positions.
Define each membership category with its requirements, dues amount, and voting or participation rights.
Set up the data entry forms and import process for existing members.

steps.description: Process new member registrations from application through onboarding.

outputs.name: registration-workflow
outputs.desc: Steps from application to active membership

outputs.name: onboarding-checklist
outputs.desc: Items to complete for each new member (orientation, directory, groups)

process: Define the registration intake: application form, required information, and sponsorship or referral if applicable.
Set up the approval process: who reviews, what criteria, and the timeline.
Create the welcome sequence: confirmation, orientation session, welcome packet, directory listing.
Assign each new member to a default communication group and suggest initial involvement opportunities.

steps.description: Manage ongoing member communications including newsletters, announcements, and the member directory.

inputs.name: registration-workflow
inputs.desc: How members are registered and categorized

outputs.name: communication-plan
outputs.desc: What is sent, to whom, how often, and through which channels

outputs.name: directory-policy
outputs.desc: What member info is shared in the directory and who can access it

process: Define the communication types: weekly newsletter, event announcements, leadership updates, prayer requests or support needs.
Set the channels and frequency for each type: email, text, bulletin board, app notification.
Create the member directory with opt-in fields (phone, email, address, photo) and access controls.
Set up segmented lists so communications reach the right groups (all members, committee members, youth families).

steps.description: Track member engagement through attendance, participation, and giving to identify active, at-risk, and disengaged members.

outputs.name: engagement-metrics
outputs.desc: What is tracked (attendance, volunteering, giving, event participation) and how it is scored

outputs.name: at-risk-criteria
outputs.desc: Thresholds that flag a member as disengaged or at risk of leaving

process: Define the engagement signals: worship attendance, group participation, volunteer service, event attendance, giving frequency.
Set up the tracking method for each signal: check-in system, sign-up sheets, giving records.
Create an engagement score that combines the signals into a single indicator per member.
Define the at-risk threshold and the follow-up action (personal outreach, invitation, pastoral visit).

steps.description: Handle membership renewals, status changes, and departures.

inputs.name: engagement-metrics
inputs.desc: How engagement is tracked and scored

outputs.name: renewal-process
outputs.desc: Timeline and steps for annual or periodic membership renewal

outputs.name: membership-report
outputs.desc: Summary of active, renewed, lapsed, and departed members

process: Define the renewal cycle: annual, ongoing, or event-triggered.
Send renewal reminders with instructions for updating contact info and confirming continued membership.
Process renewals, collect any dues, and update the database status.
Handle departures: record the reason if given, remove from active lists, send a departing acknowledgment.
Produce the membership report: total active, new this period, renewed, lapsed, departed.

description: Schedule volunteers for recurring service roles: define roles, collect availability, generate schedules, handle substitutions, and track hours.

steps.description: Define the volunteer roles, requirements, and scheduling needs for recurring services or events.

inputs.name: service-schedule
inputs.desc: The recurring events or services that need volunteers (weekly worship, monthly food bank)

inputs.name: role-list
inputs.desc: The volunteer positions to fill for each event type

outputs.name: role-definitions
outputs.desc: Each role with its description, requirements, training needed, and time commitment

outputs.name: staffing-requirements
outputs.desc: Minimum and target headcount for each role per event

process: List every volunteer role by event type: greeters, ushers, musicians, sound tech, nursery, food prep, setup, cleanup.
For each role, define the requirements: minimum age, training, background check, physical ability.
Set the time commitment: arrival time, duration, frequency (weekly, monthly, quarterly).
Set the minimum and target number of volunteers per role per event.

steps.description: Collect volunteer availability and preferences for the upcoming scheduling period.

inputs.name: role-definitions
inputs.desc: The roles available and their requirements

inputs.name: staffing-requirements
inputs.desc: How many volunteers are needed per role

outputs.name: availability-matrix
outputs.desc: Each volunteer's available dates, preferred roles, and blackout dates

outputs.name: skill-roster
outputs.desc: Volunteers matched to the roles they are qualified for

process: Send the availability survey to all active volunteers with the scheduling period dates.
Collect each volunteer's available dates, preferred roles, and any blackout dates.
Match volunteers to roles based on qualifications and preferences.
Identify gaps where available volunteers are fewer than the minimum requirement.

steps.description: Generate the volunteer schedule balancing coverage, fairness, and preferences.

outputs.name: draft-schedule
outputs.desc: The proposed schedule with volunteer assignments by date and role

outputs.name: coverage-gaps
outputs.desc: Dates or roles that remain unfilled after scheduling

process: Assign volunteers to roles and dates, distributing shifts fairly across the roster.
Respect preferences: honor blackout dates, preferred roles, and maximum frequency.
Identify remaining coverage gaps and flag them for recruitment or reassignment.
Produce the draft schedule for review before distribution.

steps.description: Send schedule confirmations and reminders to assigned volunteers.

outputs.name: confirmation-log
outputs.desc: Record of confirmations sent and responses received

outputs.name: reminder-schedule
outputs.desc: When reminders will be sent before each shift

process: Send each volunteer their assigned dates and roles with a confirmation request.
Track responses: confirmed, declined, no response.
For declined or no-response slots, find a substitute from the available roster.
Set up automatic reminders (48 hours and 2 hours before each shift).

steps.description: Handle no-shows, cancellations, and last-minute substitutions.

outputs.name: substitution-log
outputs.desc: Record of swaps, no-shows, and how each was resolved

outputs.name: updated-schedule
outputs.desc: The schedule with all substitutions applied

process: When a volunteer cancels, search the available roster for a qualified substitute.
Contact potential substitutes in priority order (least recent service, closest match).
Log the substitution: original volunteer, reason, substitute, and confirmation.
If no substitute is found, notify the event coordinator to adjust the plan.

steps.description: Track volunteer hours served for recognition, reporting, and scheduling fairness.

inputs.name: substitution-log
inputs.desc: Final record of who served each shift

outputs.name: hours-report
outputs.desc: Total hours served by each volunteer, by role, and by period

outputs.name: recognition-list
outputs.desc: Volunteers who reached milestone hours for recognition

process: Record actual attendance for each scheduled shift: served, no-show, or substituted.
Calculate hours served per volunteer for the period.
Flag volunteers who reached recognition milestones (50, 100, 250 hours).
Produce the hours report for leadership review and the next scheduling cycle's fairness input.

description: Manage giving and donations: set up donation channels, process gifts, issue acknowledgments, track giving by donor and fund, and produce year-end statements.

steps.description: Set up the channels through which the organization receives donations: online, in-person, mail, and recurring.

inputs.name: organization-profile
inputs.desc: Name, tax status, and banking information

inputs.name: fund-list
inputs.desc: The designated funds that donors can give to (general, building, missions, benevolence)

outputs.name: channel-configuration
outputs.desc: Each donation channel with its setup details and processing method

outputs.name: fund-structure
outputs.desc: The funds, their purposes, and accounting codes

process: Set up online giving: payment processor, donation page, recurring gift option, fund selection.
Set up in-person giving: offering envelopes, kiosk or card reader, counting team procedures.
Set up mail giving: PO box or address, processing workflow, deposit procedure.
Define each fund with its purpose, restrictions, and accounting code.

steps.description: Process each received gift from receipt through deposit and recording.

outputs.name: processing-procedure
outputs.desc: Step-by-step procedure for processing gifts from each channel

outputs.name: internal-controls
outputs.desc: Dual-control and segregation of duties requirements for handling funds

process: For each channel, define the receipt-to-deposit workflow: who handles, who counts, who records, who deposits.
Require dual control: at least two people handle physical gifts from collection through deposit.
Record each gift in the donor management system: donor, amount, date, fund, method, and batch number.
Reconcile the batch total against the deposit slip before closing the batch.

steps.description: Issue acknowledgment letters and tax receipts for each donation.

inputs.name: processing-procedure
inputs.desc: How gifts are processed and recorded

outputs.name: acknowledgment-templates
outputs.desc: Letter templates for different gift types (cash, stock, in-kind, recurring)

outputs.name: acknowledgment-schedule
outputs.desc: When acknowledgments are sent (immediate, weekly batch, or threshold-based)

process: Create acknowledgment templates that meet IRS requirements: organization name, tax ID, gift amount, date, and statement of no goods or services received.
Set the acknowledgment schedule: immediate for online gifts, weekly batch for checks and cash.
For non-cash gifts (stock, property, in-kind), use the appropriate template with a description but no valuation.
Send each acknowledgment and log the send date in the donor record.

steps.description: Track giving by donor and by fund to monitor progress against goals and budgets.

outputs.name: giving-dashboard
outputs.desc: Current giving totals by fund, compared against budget and prior year

outputs.name: donor-giving-history
outputs.desc: Per-donor giving record showing amounts, dates, funds, and year-to-date total

process: Aggregate giving by fund and compare against the annual budget and prior year.
Track each donor's year-to-date giving total and gift frequency.
Flag significant changes: first-time donors, lapsed donors, and large increases or decreases.
Produce the giving dashboard for leadership review.

steps.description: Produce and distribute year-end giving statements for tax purposes.

outputs.name: giving-statements
outputs.desc: Individual year-end giving statements for each donor

outputs.name: giving-summary-report
outputs.desc: Organization-wide giving summary for the year by fund and donor count

process: Pull each donor's complete giving record for the calendar year.
Generate the year-end statement with the required IRS language, itemized gifts, and annual total.
Distribute statements by the donor's preferred method (email or mail) by January 31.
Produce the organization-wide giving summary: total raised, by fund, donor count, average gift, and comparison to prior year.

description: Coordinate small groups (study, support, interest): define group types, recruit leaders, manage registrations, facilitate communication, and track engagement.

steps.description: Define the types of small groups, their purposes, and meeting structures.

inputs.name: organization-goals
inputs.desc: What the organization wants small groups to accomplish (fellowship, education, support, service)

inputs.name: member-demographics
inputs.desc: Age groups, interests, and geographic distribution of the membership

outputs.name: group-types
outputs.desc: Defined group categories with purpose, format, duration, and target audience

outputs.name: meeting-guidelines
outputs.desc: Recommended meeting frequency, duration, location, and curriculum or agenda

process: Define the group categories: study groups, support groups, interest or hobby groups, service teams, age-specific groups.
For each type, set the purpose, typical size (6 to 12), meeting frequency, and duration (semester, year-round, or open-ended).
Create meeting guidelines: recommended agenda structure, facilitation tips, and reporting requirements.
Define how groups relate to the larger organization: reporting line, resource access, and event integration.

steps.description: Recruit, screen, and train small group leaders.

inputs.name: group-types
inputs.desc: The group categories and their requirements

outputs.name: leader-roster
outputs.desc: Approved leaders with their assigned group types and training status

outputs.name: training-curriculum
outputs.desc: Leader training materials covering facilitation, pastoral care basics, and reporting

process: Identify potential leaders from active, engaged members with relevant skills or experience.
Screen candidates: interview, background check if required, and reference check.
Train leaders on facilitation, handling sensitive situations, when to escalate to pastoral staff, and reporting attendance.
Match each leader to a group type based on their gifts and interests.

steps.description: Manage member registrations into small groups.

inputs.name: leader-roster
inputs.desc: Available leaders and their group assignments

inputs.name: training-curriculum
inputs.desc: What leaders have been trained on

outputs.name: group-roster
outputs.desc: Each group with its leader, members, meeting time, and location

outputs.name: waitlist
outputs.desc: Members waiting for a spot if groups are full

process: Open registration with the group catalog: type, leader, meeting day and time, location, and description.
Allow members to select their preferred group or request a recommendation based on interests and schedule.
Cap groups at the target size and add overflow to the waitlist.
Notify leaders of their group roster and provide member contact information.

steps.description: Facilitate communication within and across small groups.

inputs.name: group-roster
inputs.desc: Members and leaders of each group

outputs.name: communication-channels
outputs.desc: The messaging platform or method for each group (group text, email list, app group)

outputs.name: leader-update-cadence
outputs.desc: How often leaders report to the organization and what they report

process: Set up the communication channel for each group: group text thread, email list, or messaging app group.
Provide leaders with a template for weekly or meeting-day communication: reminder, topic, and any prep.
Set the cadence for leader reports to the organization: attendance, concerns, and highlights.
Facilitate cross-group communication for organization-wide events or combined group activities.

steps.description: Track small group attendance and engagement, and produce the coordination report.

outputs.name: engagement-report
outputs.desc: Attendance trends, participation rates, and group health indicators

outputs.name: coordination-plan
outputs.desc: Summary of all groups, their status, and recommendations for the next period

process: Collect attendance data from leader reports for each meeting.
Calculate participation rate (attended vs. enrolled) by group and across all groups.
Flag groups with declining attendance or leader concerns for follow-up.
Produce the coordination plan: groups continuing, new groups to launch, groups to merge or retire, and leader needs.

description: Plan a weekly worship service or program: order of service, volunteer scheduling, materials preparation, rehearsal, and execution.

steps.description: Plan the order of service including music, readings, message, and announcements.

inputs.name: service-date
inputs.desc: The date and time of the service

inputs.name: theme-or-series
inputs.desc: The sermon series, liturgical season, or theme for this service

outputs.name: order-of-service
outputs.desc: The sequence of elements: prelude, welcome, songs, readings, message, offering, closing

outputs.name: content-assignments
outputs.desc: Who is responsible for each element (speaker, musicians, readers)

process: Select the scripture readings and message topic aligned with the theme or series.
Choose the songs or hymns that fit the theme and flow of the service.
Sequence the elements: prelude, welcome, opening song, prayer, readings, message, response, offering, announcements, closing song, benediction.
Assign each element to a person: speaker, worship leader, readers, prayer leader, announcer.

steps.description: Schedule the volunteers needed for this specific service (musicians, readers, ushers, tech).

outputs.name: volunteer-assignments
outputs.desc: Each volunteer role filled with a name and confirmation status

outputs.name: tech-requirements
outputs.desc: Audio, visual, and streaming needs for this service

process: List every volunteer role needed: sound operator, projector operator, live stream operator, greeters, ushers, nursery, communion servers.
Check the master volunteer schedule and fill each slot, confirming with assigned volunteers.
Identify the tech requirements: microphones, slides, video playback, live stream setup.
Send the volunteer assignments with arrival time and any special instructions.

steps.description: Prepare the materials for the service: slides, bulletins, handouts, and communion elements.

inputs.name: volunteer-assignments
inputs.desc: Confirmed volunteer roster for the service

outputs.name: presentation-file
outputs.desc: The slide deck or projection content for the service

outputs.name: printed-materials
outputs.desc: Bulletin, song sheets, handouts, and any special inserts

process: Build the slide deck: song lyrics, scripture text, sermon points, announcements, and transition slides.
Create the printed bulletin with the order of service, announcements, and response cards.
Prepare any physical materials: communion elements, offering containers, baptism supplies.
Send the presentation file to the tech team and the bulletin to the print coordinator by the deadline.

steps.description: Coordinate the rehearsal for the worship team and tech crew.

inputs.name: presentation-file
inputs.desc: The slide deck for the service

outputs.name: rehearsal-notes
outputs.desc: Adjustments made during rehearsal (timing, transitions, audio levels)

outputs.name: service-ready-checklist
outputs.desc: Confirmation that all elements are prepared and tested

process: Schedule the rehearsal: worship team sound check, tech walk-through, and run-through of transitions.
Test all audio, video, and streaming equipment during the sound check.
Walk through the full order of service noting transitions, cues, and timing.
Log any adjustments and confirm the service is ready to execute.

steps.description: Execute the service and record the outcomes for the planning archive.

outputs.name: service-record
outputs.desc: What happened: attendance, offerings collected, technical issues, and notes for improvement

outputs.name: follow-up-items
outputs.desc: Action items arising from the service (pastoral follow-ups, visitor contacts, equipment repairs)

process: Execute the service according to the order, managing transitions and timing.
Record attendance (in-person and online if streaming).
Count and record the offering.
Log any technical issues, visitor information, and follow-up items.
Produce the service record for the planning archive.

description: Plan and execute a community event: define purpose, plan logistics, recruit volunteers, promote, execute, and collect feedback.

steps.description: Define the event purpose, target audience, and success criteria.

inputs.name: event-idea
inputs.desc: The proposed event (festival, fundraiser, outreach, celebration)

inputs.name: available-budget
inputs.desc: The budget available for the event

outputs.name: event-brief
outputs.desc: Purpose, target audience, date, estimated attendance, and success metrics

outputs.name: budget-allocation
outputs.desc: How the budget is divided across venue, food, supplies, promotion, and contingency

process: Define the event purpose: fundraising, community building, outreach, celebration, or service.
Identify the target audience: members only, community open, families, youth, seniors.
Set the date, time, and estimated attendance based on past events and audience size.
Allocate the budget across categories and define the success metrics (attendance, funds raised, new contacts).

steps.description: Plan the logistics: venue, food, activities, speakers, and supplies.

outputs.name: logistics-plan
outputs.desc: Venue, layout, food plan, activity schedule, speaker lineup, and supply list

outputs.name: vendor-list
outputs.desc: External vendors or suppliers with contact info, orders, and delivery schedule

process: Select and reserve the venue (own facility or external), confirm capacity and layout.
Plan the food: catering, potluck, food trucks, or concessions with quantities and dietary accommodations.
Schedule the activities, speakers, or entertainment with time slots.
Create the supply and equipment list: tables, chairs, decorations, signage, AV, and safety items.

steps.description: Recruit and schedule volunteers for the event.

inputs.name: logistics-plan
inputs.desc: The event logistics and activity schedule

outputs.name: volunteer-roster
outputs.desc: Volunteers assigned to roles with shift times

outputs.name: volunteer-instructions
outputs.desc: Role-specific instructions and contact information

process: List every volunteer role: setup, registration, food service, activity stations, parking, cleanup, first aid.
Recruit from the membership and community, matching skills to roles.
Schedule volunteers in shifts to avoid burnout and ensure coverage for the full event.
Send each volunteer their role, shift time, arrival instructions, and the event-day contact number.

steps.description: Promote the event through internal and external channels.

outputs.name: promotion-plan
outputs.desc: Channels, timeline, and materials for promoting the event

outputs.name: registration-count
outputs.desc: Number of registrations or RSVPs received

process: Create the promotional materials: flyer, social media graphics, email announcement, and bulletin insert.
Distribute through internal channels: email list, bulletin, announcements, and social media.
If community-open, distribute externally: community boards, local media, neighborhood flyers, partner organizations.
Track registrations or RSVPs and adjust logistics if attendance projections change.

steps.description: Execute the event day and collect feedback afterward.

outputs.name: event-record
outputs.desc: Actual attendance, budget spent, issues encountered, and photos or documentation

outputs.name: feedback-summary
outputs.desc: Attendee and volunteer feedback with scores and suggestions

process: Execute setup according to the logistics plan, briefing volunteers on their roles.
Run the event: manage the schedule, handle issues as they arise, welcome attendees.
Record actual attendance and capture photos or documentation.
After the event, send a feedback survey to attendees and volunteers.
Produce the event record: actual vs. budget, attendance, feedback summary, and lessons learned.

description: Run a benevolence or assistance program: define criteria, receive applications, verify need, distribute assistance, and track spending.

steps.description: Define the benevolence program: eligibility criteria, assistance types, funding source, and limits.

inputs.name: program-budget
inputs.desc: Annual or periodic budget allocated to benevolence

inputs.name: community-needs
inputs.desc: Common needs in the community (rent, utilities, food, medical, transportation)

outputs.name: program-policy
outputs.desc: Eligibility rules, assistance types, per-request and annual limits, and approval authority

outputs.name: application-form
outputs.desc: The form applicants complete to request assistance

process: Define who can apply: members, regular attendees, community residents, or referrals from partner organizations.
List the assistance types: rent or mortgage, utilities, food, medical bills, transportation, and emergency shelter.
Set the limits: maximum per request, maximum per household per year, and total program budget.
Define the approval process: who reviews, what documentation is required, and the approval authority (pastor, committee, deacons).

steps.description: Receive and review benevolence applications.

outputs.name: application-decision
outputs.desc: Approved, denied, or referred with rationale and amount

outputs.name: verification-notes
outputs.desc: Documentation reviewed and need verification results

process: Receive the application and check completeness: contact info, description of need, supporting documents.
Verify eligibility against the program policy.
Review supporting documentation: bills, eviction notice, disconnect notice, medical statements.
Make the decision: approve (full or partial), deny with reason, or refer to an external resource.

steps.description: Distribute the approved assistance and document the disbursement.

inputs.name: application-decision
inputs.desc: Approved request with amount and type

outputs.name: disbursement-record
outputs.desc: Payment made: amount, payee, method, date, and fund source

outputs.name: applicant-notification
outputs.desc: Communication sent to the applicant about the decision and next steps

process: For approved requests, issue payment directly to the vendor (landlord, utility company, provider) rather than to the applicant.
Record the disbursement: amount, payee, check number or transfer ID, date, and which fund was charged.
Notify the applicant of the decision, amount, and how payment was made.
If denied, communicate the reason and provide referrals to other assistance resources.

steps.description: Track benevolence spending against the budget and produce the program report.

outputs.name: budget-status
outputs.desc: Spent vs. remaining by assistance type and total

outputs.name: program-report
outputs.desc: Number of requests, approvals, denials, total distributed, and remaining budget

process: Total disbursements by assistance type and compare against the allocated budget.
Track the number of unique households served and repeat requests.
Flag if spending is on pace to exhaust the budget before the period ends.
Produce the program report for the governing board: requests received, approved, denied, dollars distributed, and budget remaining.

description: Manage facility use by internal and external groups: define spaces, set policies, process bookings, manage setup and teardown, and handle insurance requirements.

steps.description: Inventory the facility spaces and equipment available for use.

inputs.name: facility-description
inputs.desc: The building or campus and its spaces (sanctuary, hall, classrooms, kitchen, grounds)

inputs.name: equipment-list
inputs.desc: Available equipment (tables, chairs, AV, kitchen, sports)

outputs.name: space-catalog
outputs.desc: Each space with capacity, features, available hours, and restrictions

outputs.name: equipment-catalog
outputs.desc: Available equipment with quantities and condition

process: List each usable space: name, capacity (seated, standing, classroom), features (kitchen access, AV, outdoor), and parking.
Note the restrictions: noise limits, hours of use, alcohol policy, decorating rules.
Inventory the equipment: tables, chairs, AV gear, kitchen equipment, sports equipment, and their condition.
Set the available hours for each space, accounting for regular programming.

steps.description: Set the policies and fees for facility use by internal and external groups.

outputs.name: use-policies
outputs.desc: Rules for facility use: who can book, fees, deposits, cancellation, cleanup, and prohibited uses

outputs.name: fee-schedule
outputs.desc: Rental fees by space, hours, and user type (member, nonprofit, commercial)

process: Define who can use the facility: members (free or reduced), nonprofits, community groups, commercial renters.
Set fees by space and user type, including the security deposit and cleaning fee.
Write the use agreement covering: liability, insurance requirements, setup and cleanup expectations, damage policy, and prohibited activities.
Define the cancellation policy and refund terms.

steps.description: Process facility booking requests from inquiry through confirmation.

inputs.name: fee-schedule
inputs.desc: Pricing by space and user type

outputs.name: booking-record
outputs.desc: Confirmed booking with date, time, space, user, fees, and signed agreement

outputs.name: booking-calendar
outputs.desc: Master calendar showing all reservations and availability

process: Receive the booking request: date, time, space, event type, expected attendance, and any special needs.
Check availability on the master calendar and confirm no conflicts with regular programming.
Send the use agreement and fee invoice; collect the signed agreement, payment, and deposit.
Confirm the booking, add it to the master calendar, and send the confirmation with access instructions.

steps.description: Manage the setup, access, and teardown for each booked event.

outputs.name: setup-instructions
outputs.desc: Room layout, equipment placement, and access details for the event

outputs.name: post-event-inspection
outputs.desc: Condition report after the event noting any damage or issues

process: Provide the room layout diagram and equipment placement instructions to the setup team or renter.
Arrange building access: keys, codes, or a host to open and close.
After the event, inspect the space: cleanliness, equipment returned, and any damage.
Document the inspection results and process any damage charges against the deposit.

steps.description: Handle liability and insurance requirements for facility use.

outputs.name: insurance-log
outputs.desc: Record of insurance certificates received and verified for each external booking

outputs.name: facility-use-report
outputs.desc: Summary of all bookings, revenue, expenses, and issues for the period

process: Require external users to provide a certificate of insurance naming the organization as additional insured.
Verify the certificate: coverage amount, dates, and additional insured endorsement.
Maintain the insurance log with certificates filed by booking.
Produce the facility use report: bookings by type, revenue collected, maintenance costs, and issues.
